ai.description: The Ashwamedh Writhing Skink reaches 6–7 cm in snout-vent length. It features a bronze-brown dorsum with a distinct dark lateral band and pale spots, characterized by a slender body and reduced limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis ashwamedhi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe bordered by a dark band, combined with a lack of keeled scales.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis ashwamedhi* is typically found in the moist deciduous forests and scrublands of the Eastern Ghats, often inhabiting leaf litter at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Ashwamedh writhing skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis ashwamedhi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–7 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis ashwamedhi* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of India, specifically recorded in the states of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
